profile.headline: AI/ML Researcher · Precision Agriculture & IoT
profile.tagline: I build machine-learning and IoT systems that help farmers make better decisions — from soil sensors in the field to models running on the edge.
profile.about:
I'm a Research Assistant at North South University working at the intersection of machine learning, computer vision and the Internet of Things, with a focus on agriculture. My work spans IoT-enabled crop recommendation, CNN-based plant disease detection, and real-time environmental monitoring of soil, weather and crop conditions.

I hold a B.Sc. in Computer Science and Engineering from North South University. Along the way I've worked across the full pipeline — collecting field data, preprocessing and feature engineering, training and evaluating models, and deploying them on low-cost hardware. I enjoy working in interdisciplinary teams and turning data into practical systems that make a real difference.

publications.title: An IoT-enabled AI system for real-time crop prediction using soil and weather data in precision agriculture
publications.authors: MD Shaifullah Sharafat, Nilavro Das Kabya, Rahimul Islam Emu, Mehrab Uddin Ahmed, Jakaria Chowdhury Onik, Mohammad Aminul Islam, Riasat Khan
publications.summary: An IoT-based crop recommendation system for Bangladesh that combines real-time soil sensor readings with weather data. Using 3,300 samples covering 22 crops and eight soil and environmental features, the study compares Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, stacking ensembles and TabNet, deploys the model on a Raspberry Pi 5 for low-latency inference, visualises data on ThingsBoard, and explains predictions with LIME.
highlights: 95.8% | Random Forest, deployed on Raspberry Pi 5
22 crops | Learned from 3,300 soil and weather samples
LIME explanations make each crop recommendation interpretable for farmers
Live sensor and weather dashboards built on ThingsBoard

projects.title: IoT-Enabled Crop Recommendation System
